text:
adrian: Quick sync — AWS / GCP EDP talks. We need firm capacity guarantees for H100/A100 across us-west and eu-west for next quarter launch. Any updates from the sales side?

emma: We asked for 120 reserved H100s in us-west1 and 80 in eu-west1, with ability to burst +30% during scheduled campaigns. Also asked for SKU failover (H100 -> A100) with capped delta $/GPU.

raj: Important: customer SLA requires <150ms p95 for model infer in us-west; if capacity is unavailable we need automatic fallbacks to dedicated pools or alternative regions w/ predictable latency. Legal wants credit language for missed capacity windows.

procurement-bot: FYI procurement checklist: attach estimated monthly commitment, preferred term (12 vs 36), invoice cadence, PO lead time, billing contact. See /docs/edp-checklist link.

maria-aws: Hi all — thanks for the summary. From AWS side we can offer an EDP with committed spend + a Capacity Reservation Addendum. Tentative terms: 12m EDP $1.2M/month -> 22% list discount; Capacity SLA: 90% availability of reserved SKUs in stated regions during business hours, with credits for each unavailable 24h window. Burst is handled via "Elastic Capacity" entitlement up to agreed headroom.

maria-aws: Caveats: H100 availability is limited in eu-west currently. We can guarantee capacity in us-west with reservations; eu-west would be on a best-effort with monthly ramp schedule. We can include a rollover credit for unused monthly capacity up to 20%.

adrian: Can we get the SLA in writing (specific formula for availability and credits)? 90% seems low for production-facing features. Need to push to 99%+ for reserved pool during business-critical windows.

emma: Also want the ability to pool capacity across regions in the contract (inventory pooling) — e.g., if eu-west can't meet a surge, we can move some workload to us-west without penalty. That mitigates regional cold-start risk.

sven-gcp: From GCP side — we have a Capacity Commitment with a Regional Reservation option. We can commit GPUs via Committed Use for GPUs + regional reservations. Proposed: 12m at commitment -> 20% off list + regional reservation guarantee: 95% availability, but H100 stock is on a rolling allocation. We can offer "Inventory Transfer" credits to move capacity between regions on a quarterly basis.

sven-gcp: Additional note: If you need strict per-hour guarantees (for launches), we recommend a mix: reserved capacity + prefunded burst credits for on-demand excess. That gives predictable budget and better availability.

chris-ops: Ops question — how soon can a reservation be turned up? We need the ability to scale up within 2–4 hours during a campaign week. If the provider needs days, it's not acceptable.

maria-aws: Turn-up time depends on stock and entitlement. With a firm reservation and PO in place, we can schedule capacity activation within 24–72 hours in us-west. eu-west could be longer. We can add a clause: expedited allocation at an additional fee (or draw from burst entitlement).

adrian: What about penalties? We need financial remedies that meaningfully offset our costs if they can't deliver capacity (not just token credits). Requesting: daily credits scaled to SLA shortfall and right to terminate reserved portion after X failed provisioning events.

maria-aws: Understood. Standard is service credit percentage (e.g., 1–5% per day of affected commitment). We can escalate to authorization for termination only after repeated breaches; need legal sign-off. Can draft language for review.

emma: Another ask: ability to reallocate unused committed spend to other services (e.g., storage or non-GPU compute) occasionally. Some providers allow limited convertible spend — that makes EDP more flexible.

sven-gcp: Convertible credits are possible but reduce discount depth. We can structure a hybrid: portion non-convertible with strong capacity guarantees, portion convertible.

raj: For negotiation tactic: push for a smaller firm reservation with stronger SLA + larger convertible bucket for burst. That limits our committed capital while getting guaranteed baseline.

procurement-bot: Reminder: capture termination windows and carry-forward terms in the draft. Also request an explicit list of SKUs covered (H100-80GB, H100-40GB, A100-40GB) and exact region codes.

chris-ops: Ops follow-up: can we get a runbook from the vendor that maps failure modes to mitigation steps? e.g., if reserved H100s are unavailable, steps to fall back to A100 with expected p95 impact and migration checklist.

maria-aws: We'll include a runbook and a "capacity playbook" appendix. It will define escalation paths, expected provision times, and supported fallbacks (with recommended instance types and price deltas).

adrian: Next steps — maria / sven, please send first-draft term sheet with explicit availability formulas, credit calculations, and regional timelines by EOD Friday. Procurement/Legal will review then. I'll schedule a 30m negotiation call next week.

maria-aws: Will do. Draft to you by Friday EOD.

sven-gcp: Sending draft for GCP options as well; will include hybrid convertible structure.

emma: Thanks — please highlight any minimum PO timing requirements. We may need to prepay one month to secure immediate activation.

procurement-bot: Logging action: vendor term sheets due by 2026-03-20. Assigned to maria-aws, sven-gcp.

adrian: Great — team, prepare a short list of fallback deploy targets (regions + latency impact) before the call.

chris-ops: On it. I'll post a short runbook and latency matrix in the call thread.

maria-aws: Note: AWS legal may require a clause limiting liability for "capacity constraints due to force majeure or supply chain". We'll try to tighten language but expect negotiation on that point.

emma: Noted. We should ask for extended notice windows for decommissioning capacity too.

adrian: Thanks everyone.
